translationRepairs: I often wished to debate with commoners on the road and hear merchants speak freely in the markets, so that word might reach your ears and awaken your heart once — even if condemned for seditious speech I would feel no regret.

I often wished to debate with commoners on the road and hear merchants voice criticism in the markets, so that word might reach your ears and awaken your heart once — even if condemned for seditious speech I would feel no regret.
商賈謗於市 pairs with 議於道; 謗 is criticism, not merely speaking freely. The revision preserves that force while supplying a natural English link to the merchants' speech.
As for the methods of Guan Yi, they are not the authority of the sage-king;
As for the methods of Yiwu, they are not the authority of the sage-king;
夷吾 is Guan Zhong’s given name Yiwu; “Guan Yi” mis-splits and truncates the two-character name present in the Chinese.
It records his name, condemning how he kept worthy scholars at a distance, favored men of punishment, and conducted himself unlike a true ruler.
It records his name, condemning how he kept worthy scholars at a distance, favored mutilated men, and conducted himself unlike a true ruler.
In the Spring and Autumn note on 閽弒吳子余祭, 昵刑人 condemns intimacy with mutilated/castrated persons, not “men of punishment.”
It records his name, condemning how he kept worthy scholars at a distance, was intimate with punishers, and had the conduct of one who is not a ruler.
It records his name, condemning how he kept worthy scholars at a distance, was intimate with mutilated men, and had the conduct of one who is not a ruler.
刑人 are persons who have undergone mutilating punishment; “punishers” invents the wrong agent class against 昵刑人.

Moreover there are those in office not according to their ability, at left and right not the worthy — wicked as the Four Evils, deceitful as Zhao Gao, treacherous as Gong and Xian — why does Your Majesty shrink from not removing them?

Moreover there are those in office not according to their ability, at left and right not the worthy — wicked as the Four Evils, deceitful as Zhao Gao, treacherous as Gong and Xian — why does Your Majesty shrink from removing them?
何憚而不去邪 asks why shrink from removing them; “shrink from not removing” reverses the force of 不去.

Your subject has heard that Yao and Yu as rulers brought all under Heaven to great order because they could employ the Nine Officers, the Four Peaks, and the Twelve Pastors — not missing the right appointment, not duplicating their tasks, not encroaching on their duties; in office only according to ability, at left and right only the worthy; Yuan Kai below though slight yet always raised, the Four Evils in court though strong yet always executed; examining security and danger, clarifying what to take and what to discard.

Your subject has heard that Yao and Yu as rulers brought all under Heaven to great order because they could employ the Nine Officers, the Four Peaks, and the Twelve Pastors — not missing the right appointment, not duplicating their tasks, not encroaching on their duties; in office only according to ability, at left and right only the worthy; the Yuan and Kai below though slight yet always raised, the Four Evils in court though strong yet always executed; examining security and danger, clarifying what to take and what to discard.
元凱 paired with 四兇 denotes the collective Eight Yuan and Eight Kai, not a personal name “Yuan Kai.”

If misfortune adds plague upon this, followed by fierce famine — Chen Sheng and Wu Guang did not arise only in Qin, the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans did not arise only in Han; this is why I vent indignation for you, clench my fists, and grieve to the point of weeping blood.

If misfortune adds plague upon this, followed by fierce famine — Chen Sheng and Wu Guang did not arise only in Qin, the Red Eyebrows and Yellow Turbans did not arise only in Han; this is why I vent indignation for you, clutch my wrist in anguish, and grieve to the point of weeping blood.
扼腕 is the classical gesture of clutching one's wrist in indignation; the revision corrects the bodily action and states its emotional force naturally.

Hearts of benevolence and righteousness are moved below, qi of peace and harmony respond above — therefore disasters do not arise, auspicious omens are preserved and arrive, the four directions reach tranquility, the ten thousand things all succeed.

Hearts of benevolence and righteousness are moved below, qi of peace and harmony respond above — therefore disasters do not arise, auspicious omens arrive in succession, the four directions reach tranquility, and the ten thousand things all succeed.
休祥存臻 is the omen phrase equivalent to 荐臻 (successive arrival); “are preserved and arrive” invents a preserve sense for 存 that the parallel omen idiom does not support.
What your subject earlier called "broad sowing and planting lies in observing food strength."
What your subject earlier called "broad sowing and planting lies in observing the people's capacity to produce food."
視食力, clarified by the following 民勤於食 material, concerns the people’s food-producing capacity; “food strength” is an opaque calque that obscures that policy sense.
reflecting on the hundred measures' need for correctness — it lies in selecting the myriad offices and personally entrusting them, letting them focus on keeping to their duties;
reflecting on the hundred measures' need for correctness — it lies in selecting the myriad officials and entrusting them, letting them focus on keeping to their duties;
Old Tangshu’s parallel and other Xin Tangshu editions read 擇庶官而任之 with the neighboring 以任之 lines; “personally” invents a face-to-face sense from 面, and 庶官 here are officials.
reflecting on the hundred measures' need for correctness — it lies in selecting the myriad offices and personally entrusting them, letting them focus on keeping to their duties;
reflecting on the hundred measures' need for correctness — it lies in selecting the myriad officials and entrusting them, letting them focus on keeping to their duties;
Same parallel as the idiomatic line: authoritative witnesses have 而任之, so literal “personally entrusting” invents meaning from the 面 variant while 庶官 are the officials entrusted.

Your subject is not unaware that when words issue disaster responds, when plans are carried out the body is punished — broadly grieving the altars' peril, mourning the living people's regret: how could he bear to temporize with the times' taboos and steal one life of Your Majesty's favor?

Your subject is not unaware that when words issue disaster responds, when plans are carried out the body is punished — broadly grieving the altars' peril, mourning the living people's suffering: how could he bear to temporize with the times' taboos and steal one life of Your Majesty's favor?
哀生人之悔, paired with 痛社稷之危 and matching the idiomatic “suffering,” uses 悔 as the people’s misery/calamity, not emotional regret.
